land.text: the part of Donetsk Oblast held by the separatists: Donetsk, Horlivka and the eastern districts

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Ukraine row (1992-2024) draws the whole oblast as Ukrainian; the pages opened give no area for the part the DPR held.

land.text: the DPR as annexed by Russia on 30 September 2022 (the DPR's claimed borders; about 55% of Donetsk Oblast by June 2022)

successors.note: 'Putin announced the annexation of the DPR, along with the LPR and two other Ukrainian oblasts'; Russia claimed the DPR's borders, not the entire oblast. Commentators widely described the referendum of 23-27 September 2022 as a sham (DPR page).

capitals.name: Donetsk
capitals.note: The republic was declared in the Donetsk regional government building (7 April 2014); the page names no capital in the summary read. Coordinates are Donetsk's.

rulers.name: Alexander Zakharchenko, head
rulers.title: Head of the DPR
rulers.note: 4 November 2014 to 31 August 2018, killed by a bomb in a Donetsk cafe. The page names no head for April to November 2014.

rulers.name: Denis Pushilin, head
rulers.title: Head of the DPR
rulers.note: From 7 September 2018, acting until 20 November 2018; still head at the annexation.

correction.text: the area around Donetsk and Horlivka with Debaltseve, held by the separatists after the retreats of June and July 2014 and the capture of Debaltseve in February 2015 (a reading: the pages give no boundary, area or map)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Neither the DPR page nor the War in Donbas page gives an area or a front line; the shape is circles around Donetsk (50 km), Horlivka (35 km) and Debaltseve (15 km) cut to the oblast, about 8,900 km2 at the grid against the oblast's 27,800 km2 at the grid. The line of contact was static from early 2015 (trench warfare) to February 2022.

correction.text: about 55% of Donetsk Oblast: 'by June 2022 around 55% of Donetsk Oblast' was under Russian and DPR control, before the annexation of 30 September 2022

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the war year. The circles (Donetsk 60 km, Horlivka 40 km, Mariupol 35 km, a 30 km circle at 38.05 E 47.9 N) were tuned so the shape holds about 54% of the oblast's grid cells, matching the page's 55%; where the front lay is not on the pages opened, so the shape is a fit to a number, not a map.

region.text: the separatist-held parts of Donetsk Oblast in April-June 2014: Donetsk and Horlivka, Sloviansk and Kramatorsk, Mariupol

ledger.note: 7 April 2014: separatists proclaim the Donetsk People's Republic. After occupying the regional government building on 6 April, the separatists 'voted to declare an independent Donetsk People's Republic' on 7 April; the regional council had not agreed. A referendum on 11 May 2014 claimed 89% for self-rule (unrecognised) and on 12 May the People's Soviet declared Donetsk province a sovereign state. Confidence lowered to 2 by the eu-22-x reviewer: the region adds circles at Kramatorsk, Mariupol and Debaltseve, and neither page says these were held in April 2014.

region.text: Donbas, the Donetsk Oblast war zone

ledger.note: 12 April 2014: the war in Donbas begins. A Russian paramilitary unit 'crossed the border from Russia into Ukraine and seized the strategic town of Sloviansk' on 12 April 2014 (the DPR page adds Kramatorsk); Ukraine began its 'Anti-Terrorist Operation' on 15 April.

13 June 2014: Ukraine retakes Mariupol. 'Ukrainian troops and the National Guard retook Mariupol and declared it the provisional capital of Donetsk Oblast.' The pages do not say when the separatists took it.
5 July 2014: Ukraine retakes Sloviansk and Kramatorsk. 'Government forces retook Sloviansk'; 'Sporadic fighting continued until 5 July, when the insurgents withdrew from Kramatorsk.'

February 2015: Debaltseve falls to the separatists. 'Immediately after Minsk II, Russian forces renewed their offensive on Debaltseve and forced Ukraine's military to withdraw' (no day given); Donetsk Airport had fallen in January 2015.

region.text: Donbas, the Donetsk Oblast war zone

ledger.note: 12 February 2015: Minsk II. 'On 12 February 2015, DPR and LPR leaders Alexander Zakharchenko and Igor Plotnitsky signed Minsk II', calling for decentralisation and the reintegration of rebel-held territory into Ukraine, which the Rada never ratified; the war page describes static trench warfare after the September 2014 Minsk agreement, 'dozens killed monthly'.

24 February 2022: the full-scale invasion. Russia recognised the DPR and the LPR on 21 February 2022 and 'three days later, on 24 February, it launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine', subsuming the Donbas war.

region.text: the additional part of Donetsk Oblast taken in 2022, to about 55% of the oblast

ledger.note: By June 2022: Russian and DPR forces hold about 55% of Donetsk Oblast. The page gives the share, not the towns or the day; the month is the page's 'by June'.
30 September 2022: the republic ends in annexation; the fighting for the rest of Donetsk Oblast continues as Russia against Ukraine (the russian-federation dossier).

region.text: the DPR with its 2022 gains, to the Russian Federation

ledger.note: 30 September 2022: Russia announces the annexation of the DPR. After a referendum of 23-27 September 2022 that commentators called a sham, 'Putin announced the annexation of the DPR, along with the LPR and two other Ukrainian oblasts' in an address to the Russian parliament; Russia claimed the DPR's borders, not the entire oblast.

wars.name: War in Donbas
wars.outcome: Ukraine retook Mariupol (13 June 2014) and Sloviansk and Kramatorsk (5 July 2014); Minsk II was agreed on 12 February 2015 and the front stayed static until Russia recognised the DPR and LPR on 21 February 2022 and invaded on 24 February.
wars.note: The page gives no territorial percentage or area for the separatist zone; it counts 6.1 million people in the two oblasts in 2011 and 2 million refugees.

wars.name: Russian invasion of Ukraine
wars.outcome: Russia and the DPR held about 55% of Donetsk Oblast by June 2022; Russia announced the annexation of the DPR on 30 September 2022.
wars.note: Only the Donetsk part is read here; the invasion's other fronts belong to the Ukraine and Russia dossiers.

certainty.note: A line of contact, static from 2015 to February 2022; the pages give no coordinates.

sources.title: Donetsk People's Republic
sources.note: 7 April 2014, 11-12 May 2014, Minsk II, heads of the DPR, Russian recognition 21 February 2022, 55% by June 2022, annexation 30 September 2022; no area or capital.

sources.title: War in Donbas
sources.note: 12 April 2014 Sloviansk, 13 June 2014 Mariupol, 5 July 2014, January and February 2015, static front to 2022; no area or percentage.

notes: A separatist state Cliopatria lacks (its Ukraine row, 1992-2024, draws the oblast whole). Type rebel (rule 5). The pages opened are silent on the area and the line of contact, so every shape here is a reading: circles around towns the pages name. Not covered by the pages: the 24 May 2014 Treaty of Union ('New Russia'), Minsk I's day (September 2014, no day), the Ilovaisk battle (August 2014), the dates the separatists took Mariupol and Donetsk Airport, the 2022 towns (Mariupol, Volnovakha, Bakhmut and others), the leaders from April to November 2014. The Russian occupation of the 2014-2022 DPR and Russian recognition on 21 February 2022 (with 'peacekeeping' troops) belong to the Russian dossier as a client relation. Gazetteer: Natural Earth names the oblast "Donets'k"; Debaltseve, Ilovaisk, Sloviansk and Volnovakha are not in places (circles used).
